meta.title: What happens when someone uploads a 100 MB file

views.label: One Bun process
views.note: Shares in-memory state (in-flight upload set, login rate limiter), so exactly one instance may run

messages.label: createUpload(name, size, who)
messages.note: Arrives as POST /api/workspaces/:id/uploads from the browser, via Cloudflare and the tunnel; 'who' is the signed-in key holder, never a name the browser claims.

messages.label: check quota, insert upload row
messages.note: Inserted synchronously, before any await, so two simultaneous uploads cannot both pass the quota check.

messages.label: appendChunk(offset n, ≤8 MiB)
messages.note: A PATCH with an Upload-Offset header. 409 with the server's offset if n is not what it expects; the browser resumes from there.

messages.label: write bytes at offset n · file
insert file, mark upload done
messages.note: One transaction, which first re-checks that the upload still exists, so a workspace deleted mid-rename cannot leave an orphan row.

cards.title: The short answer
items: The browser never sends the file in one request
It asks the server for an upload id, then sends 8 MiB chunks, each stamped with the byte offset it starts at
the server writes each chunk at that offset and records progress, and on the last byte renames the temp file into place and records the file in one transaction

cards.title: Not shown here
items: The browser, Cloudflare and the tunnel, which carry every step's request the same way (see the overview)

cards.title: Constraints
items: No request body may exceed 100 MB, so files travel in 8 MiB chunks: Cloudflare's free and pro plans reject larger bodies with a 413; the server caps bodies at chunk size + 1 MiB to match
